# Simplyblock Documentation

> Simplyblock is a cloud-native, software-defined storage platform that provides NVMe-over-TCP block storage for Kubernetes and Linux, with erasure coding, snapshots, clones, and multi-tenancy.

Every page of this documentation is available as Markdown: append `.md` to any page URL, or request the page with an `Accept: text/markdown` header. The complete documentation as a single file: https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/llms-full.txt

## Overview

- [Home](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/index.md): Home: Welcome to the Simplyblock Documentation, the comprehensive resource for understanding, deploying, and managing simplyblock's cloud-native platform.

## Important Notes

- [Important Notes](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/important-notes/index.md): Important Notes: Simplyblock is a high-performance distributed block storage optimized for Kubernetes that is compatible with any Linux.
- [Terminology](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/important-notes/terminology.md): Terminology: A simplyblock storage cluster is a group of interconnected storage nodes that work together to provide a scalable, fault-tolerant, and.
- [Acronyms & Abbreviations](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/important-notes/acronyms.md): Reference table of Simplyblock acronyms and abbreviations used across architecture, deployment, operations, Kubernetes, NVMe, and security documentation.
- [Documentation Conventions](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/important-notes/documentation-conventions.md): Documentation Conventions: Features in simplyblock are released when reaching general availability.
- [Known Issues](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/important-notes/known-issues.md): Known Issues: is shown by lsblk. But when remounting the filesystem with the option to resize, it fails.
- [Contributing](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/important-notes/contributing.md): Contributing: Simplyblock's documentation is publicly available, and contributions from the community to improve clarity, fix errors, and enhance it are welcome.

## Architecture

- [Architecture](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/index.md): Architecture: Simplyblock is a cloud-native, software-defined storage platform designed for high performance, scalability, and resilience.
- [What is Simplyblock?](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/what-is-simplyblock.md): What is Simplyblock?: Simplyblock is a high-performance, distributed storage orchestration layer designed for cloud-native environments.
- [Simplyblock Architecture](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/simplyblock-architecture.md): Simplyblock Architecture: Simplyblock is a cloud-native, distributed block storage platform designed to deliver scalable, high-performance, and resilient.
- [Performance and QoS](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/storage-performance-and-qos.md): Performance and QoS: Storage performance can be categorized by latency (the aggregate response time of an I/O request from the host to the storage system) and.
- [High Availability and Fault Tolerance](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/high-availability-fault-tolerance.md): High Availability and Fault Tolerance: Simplyblock is designed to provide enterprise-grade high availability (HA) and fault tolerance for enterprise and.
- [Concepts](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/index.md): Understanding the fundamental concepts behind simplyblock is essential for effectively utilizing its distributed storage architecture.
- [Concepts / Simplyblock Cluster](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/simplyblock-cluster.md): Simplyblock Cluster: The simplyblock storage platform consists of three different types of cluster nodes and belongs to the control plane or storage plane.
- [Concepts / Storage Pooling](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/storage-pooling.md): Storage pooling is a technique used in distributed data storage systems to aggregate multiple storage devices into a single, unified storage resource.
- [Concepts / Logical Volumes](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/logical-volumes.md): Logical Volumes (LVs) in Simplyblock are virtual NVMe devices that provide scalable, high-performance storage within a distributed storage cluster.
- [Concepts / NVMe Namespaces And Subsystems](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/nvme-namespaces-and-subsystems.md): NVMe Namespaces And Subsystems: Connecting to a storage volume, both locally and via NVMe-oF, requires a subsystem and a namespace.
- [Concepts / NVMe over Fabrics Security](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/nvmf-security.md): NVMe-oF security in simplyblock provides host access control, DH-HMAC-CHAP authentication, and TLS/PSK encryption for NVMe-oF connections.
- [Concepts / Persistent Volumes](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/persistent-volumes.md): Persistent Volumes (PVs) in Kubernetes provide a mechanism for managing storage resources independently of individual Pods.
- [Concepts / External Key Management](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/external-key-management.md): How simplyblock encrypts data at rest against an external key management system, and what separation of duty, key rotation, and audit that buys.
- [Concepts / Hyper-Converged](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/hyper-converged.md): Hyper-converged storage is a key component of hyper-converged infrastructure (HCI), where compute, storage, and networking resources are tightly integrated into.
- [Concepts / Disaggregated](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/disaggregated.md): Disaggregated storage represents a modern approach to distributed storage architectures, where compute and storage resources are decoupled.
- [Concepts / Snapshots and Clones](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/snapshots-clones.md): Snapshots and Clones: Volume snapshots and volume clones are essential data management features in distributed storage systems that enable data protection.
- [Concepts / Erasure Coding](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/erasure-coding.md): Erasure coding is a data protection mechanism used in distributed storage systems to enhance fault tolerance and optimize storage efficiency.
- [Concepts / Linux Block Devices (lblk)](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/linux-block-devices.md): How simplyblock clusters use arbitrary Linux block devices, such as SAS or SATA SSDs and cloud volumes, instead of NVMe PCIe devices.
- [Concepts / Automatic Rebalancing](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/automatic-rebalancing.md): Automatic rebalancing is a fundamental feature of distributed data storage systems designed to maintain an even distribution of data across storage nodes.
- [Concepts / Volume Migration](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/volume-migration.md): How simplyblock separates front and back storage, and how the backing logical volume of a volume moves between storage nodes during a migration.
- [Concepts / Failure Domains](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/failure-domains.md): How simplyblock failure domains group storage nodes by rack, cabinet, or availability zone and constrain data, journal, and failover-path placement.
- [Concepts / Replication](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/architecture/concepts/replication.md): Asynchronous replication between simplyblock clusters for multi-site disaster recovery, continuously transferring volume snapshots to a target cluster.

- [Deployment Preparation](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/deployment-preparation/index.md): Deployment Preparation: Proper deployment planning is essential for ensuring the performance, scalability, and resilience of a simplyblock storage cluster.
- [Hardware Requirements](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/deployment-preparation/hardware-requirements.md): Minimum vCPU, RAM, NVMe device, network, and boot disk requirements for simplyblock storage nodes and control plane nodes, per deployment model.

- [Cloud Instance Recommendations](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/deployment-preparation/cloud-instance-recommendations.md): Cloud Instance Recommendations: Simplyblock has been tested on and recommends the following instance types.
- [Erasure Coding Scheme](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/deployment-preparation/erasure-coding-scheme.md): Choosing the appropriate erasure coding scheme is crucial when deploying a simplyblock storage cluster, as it directly impacts data redundancy, storage.
- [Cluster Deployment Options](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/deployment-preparation/cluster-deployment-options.md): Cluster Deployment Options: The following options can be set when creating a cluster. This applies to both plain Linux and Kubernetes deployments.
- [NUMA Considerations](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/deployment-preparation/numa-considerations.md): NUMA Considerations: Modern multi-socket servers use a memory architecture called NUMA (Non-Uniform Memory Access){:target="_blank" rel="noopener"}.
- [Air Gap Installation](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/deployment-preparation/air-gap/index.md): Air Gap Installation: Simplyblock can be installed in an air-gapped environment.
- [Data Migration](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/deployment-preparation/data-migration/index.md): Migrate data to Simplyblock using block-level cloning or file-level transfer methods, with practical guidance for tooling, planning, and validation.

## Kubernetes

- [Kubernetes](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/index.md): Kubernetes: Simplyblock runs natively on Kubernetes, where it is deployed and managed by the simplyblock operator through Custom Resource Definitions.
- [Install Simplyblock](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/index.md): Install Simplyblock on Kubernetes using the simplyblock operator, which manages the full lifecycle of clusters, storage nodes, pools, and the CSI driver via CRDs.
- [Install Simplyblock / Control Plane Cluster Architecture](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/management-cluster-architecture.md): A deep dive into the simplyblock control plane. The control plane foundation installed via Helm orchestrates an infinite number of storage clusters.
- [Install Simplyblock / Install Simplyblock Operator](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/k8s-control-plane.md): Install the simplyblock Kubernetes operator via Helm. The operator manages the full lifecycle of simplyblock clusters, storage nodes, pools, and the CSI driver.
- [Install Simplyblock / Securing the Control Plane](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/security.md): Configure mTLS for simplyblock control plane communication and offload at-rest encryption keys to an external KMS (HashiCorp Vault or OpenBao).
- [Install Simplyblock / Create a Storage Cluster](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/k8s-storage-plane.md): Deploy simplyblock storage nodes, storage pools, and the CSI driver on Kubernetes using the simplyblock operator CRDs.
- [Install Simplyblock / Install Simplyblock CSI (only)](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/install-csi.md): Install Simplyblock CSI: Simplyblock provides a seamless integration with Kubernetes through its Kubernetes CSI driver.
- [Install Simplyblock / OpenShift](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/openshift.md): When installing simplyblock on OpenShift, the process is very similar to Kubernetes, with one key difference, OpenShift requires explicitly granting the.
- [Install Simplyblock / SUSE Rancher and RKE2](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/rancher.md): Installing simplyblock into RKE2 or K3s clusters managed by SUSE Rancher, including the permissions required on CIS-hardened clusters.
- [Install Simplyblock / Talos](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/installation/talos.md): Talos: Talos Linux is a minimal Linux distribution optimized for Kubernetes.
- [Usage](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/index.md): Kubernetes CSI: Simplyblock integrates seamlessly with Kubernetes through its Container Storage Interface (CSI) driver, enabling dynamic provisioning and.
- [Usage / Storage Class](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/storage-class.md): Storage Class: A Kubernetes StorageClass defines the way dynamic storage provisioning is handled within a cluster.
- [Usage / Provisioning](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/provisioning.md): Provisioning a new PersistentVolume using simplyblock's Kubernetes CSI driver integration requires at least one StorageClass to be set up.
- [Usage / Volume Encryption](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/volume-encryption.md): Encrypt simplyblock logical volumes at rest using the AES_XTS crypto bdev. Keys are managed by the cluster and can optionally be offloaded to an external KMS.
- [Usage / Automatic Volume Placement](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/volume-placement.md): Reference for the PVC annotations and StorageCluster fields that control which storage node becomes a new volume's primary node.
- [Usage / Snapshotting](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/snapshotting.md): Snapshotting: Kubernetes PersistentVolumes backed by simplyblock can be instantly snapshotted.
- [Usage / Cloning](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/cloning.md): Cloning: Kubernetes PersistentVolumes, backed by simplyblock, can be instantly cloned.
- [Usage / Expanding](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/expanding.md): Expanding a Persistent Volume (PV) in Kubernetes allows for increasing the size of a volume without downtime, ensuring applications continue running with.
- [Usage / Removing](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/removing.md): Removing: A simplyblock-managed logical volume which is connected to a Kubernetes PersistentVolumeClaim is targeted to Kubernetes' automatic lifecycle.
- [Usage / Defining Quality of Service](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/usage/quality-of-service.md): Defining Quality of Service: Simplyblock's Kubernetes CSI driver supports Quality of Service (QoS) to define minimum guaranteed performance characteristics of a.
- [Operations](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/index.md): Overview of the operations of a simplyblock deployment on Kubernetes: the cluster and storage node lifecycle, data protection, monitoring, and security.
- [Operations / Cluster](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/index.md): Operate a simplyblock storage cluster on Kubernetes: request cluster actions, restart it node by node, upgrade it, and set its data placement.
- [Operations / Cluster / Storage Cluster Actions](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/cluster-actions.md): Trigger cluster-wide lifecycle operations on a simplyblock storage cluster through the action field of the StorageCluster resource and track their outcome.
- [Operations / Cluster / Activating a Storage Cluster](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/activating-a-cluster.md): Activate a simplyblock storage cluster on Kubernetes with the activate action, and learn when the operator activates a cluster on its own.
- [Operations / Cluster / Shutting Down a Storage Cluster](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/shutting-down-a-cluster.md): Suspend an entire simplyblock storage cluster on Kubernetes with the shutdown action, and learn what it means for the volumes the cluster serves.
- [Operations / Cluster / Starting a Storage Cluster](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/starting-a-cluster.md): Bring a suspended simplyblock storage cluster on Kubernetes back into service with the start action, and follow the rebalancing that may follow it.
- [Operations / Cluster / Restarting a Storage Cluster](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/restarting-a-cluster.md): Restart an entire simplyblock storage cluster on Kubernetes with the restart action, which sequences a shutdown and a start, and follow its two legs.
- [Operations / Cluster / Rolling Restart](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/rolling-restart.md): Restart every storage node of a simplyblock cluster in sequence with the node-recycle action, optionally refreshing the storage-node pod on each worker.
- [Operations / Cluster / Upgrading a Cluster](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/cluster-upgrade.md): Upgrade the simplyblock operator, control plane, and CSI driver with Helm, then roll the new storage-node image across the storage plane one node at a time.
- [Operations / Cluster / Managing Failure Domains](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/failure-domains.md): Enable failure-domain mode on a simplyblock cluster and assign Kubernetes workers to fault groups so erasure-coding chunks are spread across racks or zones.
- [Operations / Cluster / Configuring Node Affinity](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/cluster/node-affinity.md): Enable node affinity on a simplyblock cluster so a volume's data stays local to the storage node that owns it, and combine it with per-PVC placement.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/index.md): Operate the storage nodes of a simplyblock cluster on Kubernetes: request node actions, move a node to another worker, remove it, or replace it.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Storage Node Actions](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/storage-node-actions.md): Request an operation against a single simplyblock storage node with a StorageNodeOps resource, and track it through the phases of its status.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Shutting Down a Storage Node](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/shutting-down-a-storage-node.md): Stop a single simplyblock storage node with the shutdown action of a StorageNodeOps resource, and learn the conditions that refuse a graceful shutdown.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Restarting a Storage Node](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/restarting-a-storage-node.md): Restart a single simplyblock storage node with the restart action of a StorageNodeOps resource, optionally forced and reattaching its volumes.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Suspending a Storage Node](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/suspending-a-storage-node.md): Suspend a single simplyblock storage node so that no new volume is placed on it, while it keeps serving the volumes it already holds.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Resuming a Storage Node](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/resuming-a-storage-node.md): Return a suspended simplyblock storage node to normal service with the resume action of a StorageNodeOps resource, so new volumes are placed on it again.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Replacing a Storage Node](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/replacing-a-storage-node.md): Replace the host under a simplyblock storage node, or retire a node and add a replacement, without making the logical volumes it owns inaccessible.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Migrating a Storage Node](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/migrating-a-storage-node.md): Relocate a simplyblock storage node onto a different Kubernetes worker with the migrate action, keeping its backend identity, devices, and logical volumes.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Removing a Storage Node](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/removing-a-storage-node.md): Drain and remove a simplyblock storage node with the remove action, which evacuates its volumes onto the remaining nodes before the node leaves the cluster.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Coordinated Worker Node Drain](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/node-drain-coordination.md): How the Simplyblock operator automatically protects storage availability during Kubernetes node maintenance such as cordon, drain, and rolling OS upgrades.
- [Operations / Volumes](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/volumes/index.md): Operate simplyblock volumes on Kubernetes: migrate the backing logical volume, reclaim unused blocks, and recover a workload after a path loss.
- [Operations / Volumes / Volume Migration](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/volumes/volume-migration.md): How the Simplyblock Operator migrates the backing logical volume of a volume between storage nodes, manually or automatically when a node is drained.
- [Operations / Volumes / Trimming a Filesystem](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/volumes/trimming.md): Trimming a Filesystem: Filesystem trimming is the process of informing the underlying storage system about unused blocks, allowing simplyblock to reclaim and.
- [Operations / Volumes / Recovering from Path Loss](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/volumes/path-loss-recovery.md): How the simplyblock CSI node plugin restores NVMe-oF paths after a storage node outage, and how to opt a workload into an automatic pod restart.
- [Operations / Scaling](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/scaling/index.md): Scale a simplyblock cluster on Kubernetes by enrolling additional workers as storage nodes, and control how many of them are provisioned at a time.
- [Operations / Scaling / Expanding a Storage Cluster](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/scaling/expanding-storage-cluster.md): Add storage nodes to a running simplyblock cluster on Kubernetes with an expansion StorageNodeSet, and follow the integration of every new node.
- [Operations / Scaling / Parallel Storage Node Addition](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/scaling/parallel-node-addition.md): How the Simplyblock operator adds storage nodes in parallel while preserving FoundationDB fault tolerance with sequential adds for FDB-hosting workers.
- [Operations / Data Protection](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/data-protection/index.md): Protect the data of a simplyblock cluster on Kubernetes with snapshot backups to object storage, asynchronous replication, and FoundationDB backups.
- [Operations / Data Protection / Backup and Recovery](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/data-protection/backup-recovery.md): Snapshot-based backup and recovery to Amazon S3 or S3-compatible object storage, managed through Kubernetes CRDs or the Simplyblock CLI.
- [Operations / Data Protection / Asynchronous Replication](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/data-protection/asynchronous-replication.md): Configure snapshot-based asynchronous replication between simplyblock clusters with the ReplicationPair, ReplicationPolicy, and ReplicationOps resources.
- [Operations / Data Protection / FoundationDB Backup and Restore](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/data-protection/foundationdb-backup.md): Back up and restore the FoundationDB key-value store behind the simplyblock control plane with the FoundationDBBackup and FoundationDBRestore CRDs.
- [Operations / Monitoring](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/monitoring/index.md): Monitoring the health, performance, and resource utilization of a Simplyblock cluster is crucial for ensuring optimal operation, early issue detection, and.
- [Operations / Monitoring / Cluster Health](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/monitoring/cluster-health.md): Cluster Health: A simplyblock cluster consists of interconnected management nodes (control plane) and storage nodes (storage plane) working together to deliver.
- [Operations / Monitoring / Logical Volume Conditions](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/monitoring/lvol-conditions.md): Logical Volume Conditions: Logical volumes are the core storage abstraction in simplyblock, representing high-performance, distributed NVMe block devices backed.
- [Operations / Monitoring / Alerting](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/monitoring/alerts.md): Simplyblock uses Grafana to configure and manage alerting rules By default, Grafana is configured to send alerts to Slack channels.
- [Operations / Monitoring / Accessing Grafana](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/monitoring/accessing-grafana.md): Accessing Grafana: Simplyblock's control plane includes a Prometheus, Grafana, and Graylog installation Grafana retrieves metric data from Prometheus, including.

- [Operations / Security](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/security/index.md): Secure a simplyblock deployment on Kubernetes: authenticate and encrypt the NVMe-oF transport, encrypt volumes, and isolate tenants from each other.
- [Operations / Security / Host Authentication and Encryption](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/kubernetes/operations/security/authentication-encryption.md): Configure NVMe-oF host access control, DH-HMAC-CHAP authentication, and TLS/PSK encryption on Kubernetes through the StoragePool custom resource.

## Non-Kubernetes

- [Non-Kubernetes](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/index.md): Non-Kubernetes: Simplyblock does not require Kubernetes. A full storage cluster can be deployed on plain Linux hosts using Docker.
- [Install Simplyblock](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/installation/index.md): Install Simplyblock on Linux: Installing simplyblock for production on plain Linux (Docker) requires a few components to be installed.
- [Install Simplyblock / Install Control Plane](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/installation/install-cp.md): Install Control Plane: The first step when installing simplyblock on plain Linux (Docker), is to install the control plane.
- [Install Simplyblock / Install Storage Plane](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/installation/install-sp.md): Install Storage Plane: The installation of a storage plane requires a functioning control plane.
- [Install Simplyblock / Deploy with Linux Block Devices](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/installation/linux-block-devices.md): Deploying a simplyblock cluster on Linux block devices: cluster creation in lblk mode, device selection by name or serial, and node addition.
- [Install Simplyblock / Storage Network Multipathing](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/installation/storage-network-multipathing.md): Configure NVMe-oF multipathing over two independent storage networks as an alternative to a bonded, highly available network.
- [Plain Linux Initiators](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/linux-initiators/index.md): Plain Linux Initiators: Simplyblock storage can be attached over the network to Linux hosts which are not running Kubernetes, Proxmox, or OpenStack.
- [OpenStack Integration](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/openstack/index.md): OpenStack Integration: This driver is still not part of the official OpenStack support matrix.
- [Proxmox Integration](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/proxmox/index.md): Proxmox Integration: Proxmox Virtual Environment (Proxmox VE) is an open-source server virtualization platform that integrates KVM-based virtual machines and.

- [Usage / Snapshotting a Logical Volume](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/usage/snapshotting.md): Snapshotting a Logical Volume: Snapshots in simplyblock provide point-in-time copies of logical Volumes (LVs), allowing for backup, recovery, or cloning.
- [Usage / Cloning a Logical Volume](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/usage/cloning.md): Cloning a logical Volume (LV) in simplyblock creates a writable, independent copy-on-write clone of an existing volume.

- [Usage / Removing a Logical Volume](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/usage/removing.md): Removing a logical Volume (LV) in simplyblock permanently deletes the volume and its associated data from the cluster.
- [Usage / Encrypting a Logical Volume](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/usage/encrypting.md): Encrypting a Logical Volume: Simplyblock supports encryption of logical volumes (LVs) to protect data at rest, ensuring that sensitive information remains.
- [Usage / Defining Quality of Service](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/usage/quality-of-service.md): Defining Quality of Service: Simplyblock allows Quality of Service (QoS) limits to be applied to logical volumes (LVs) to control performance by defining.
- [Operations](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/index.md): Overview of the operations of a simplyblock deployment outside Kubernetes: the cluster and storage node lifecycle, volumes, data protection, and monitoring.
- [Operations / Cluster](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/cluster/index.md): Operate a simplyblock storage cluster outside Kubernetes: upgrade it, group its storage nodes into failure domains, and set where volume data is placed.
- [Operations / Cluster / Upgrading a Cluster](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/cluster/cluster-upgrade.md): Upgrading a Cluster: Simplyblock clusters consist of two independent parts: a control plane with management nodes, and a storage plane with storage nodes.
- [Operations / Cluster / Managing Failure Domains](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/cluster/failure-domains.md): Deploy and operate a simplyblock storage cluster with failure domains: cluster creation, node tagging, balance rules, expansion, and node removal.
- [Operations / Cluster / Configure Node Affinity](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/cluster/node-affinity.md): Configure Node Affinity: Simplyblock features node affinity, sometimes also referred to as data locality.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/index.md): Operate the storage nodes of a simplyblock cluster outside Kubernetes: restart a node, replace or relocate it, and find the node serving a failover path.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Stopping and Manually Restarting a Storage Node](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/manual-restarting-nodes.md): Stopping and Manually Restarting a Storage Node: In these cases, a manual restart is required Nodes can only be restarted from offline state!.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Replacing a Storage Node](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/replacing-storage-node.md): Replacing a Storage Node: A simplyblock storage cluster is designed to be always up.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Migrating a Storage Node](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/migrating-storage-node.md): Migrating a Storage Node: Simplyblock storage clusters are designed as always-on.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Finding the Secondary Node](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/find-secondary-node.md): Finding the Secondary Node: Simplyblock, in high-availability mode, creates two connections per logical volume: a primary and a secondary connection.
- [Operations / Storage Nodes / Linux Block Device Operations](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/storage-nodes/lblk-device-operations.md): Operating lblk-mode clusters: node restarts with serial-based device resolution, adding block devices to a node, and handling failed devices.
- [Operations / Volumes](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/volumes/index.md): Operate simplyblock logical volumes outside Kubernetes: migrate one between storage nodes, reconnect it, reclaim blocks, and limit its IOPS and throughput.
- [Operations / Volumes / Volume Migration](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/volumes/volume-migration.md): Migrate a logical volume between storage nodes with the simplyblock CLI: pre-create, client connect, continue, monitor, and cancel.
- [Operations / Volumes / Reconnecting Logical Volume](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/volumes/reconnect-nvme-device.md): Reconnecting Logical Volume: After outages of storage nodes, primary and secondary NVMe over Fabrics connections may need to be re-established.
- [Operations / Volumes / Trimming a Filesystem](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/volumes/trimming.md): Trimming a Filesystem: Filesystem trimming is the process of informing the underlying storage system about unused blocks, allowing simplyblock to reclaim and.
- [Operations / Volumes / Quality of Service Limits](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/volumes/limiting-iops-and-throughput.md): Quality of Service Limits: Quality of Service (QoS) limits (IOPS, Read, Write, and ReadWrite limits) can be chosen on both volume and pool level.
- [Operations / Volumes / QoS Service Classes](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/volumes/qos-service-classes.md): QoS Service Classes are managing cluster QUOTAS and ensure that all volumes within a class achieve their respective quota.
- [Operations / Scaling](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/scaling/index.md): Scale a simplyblock cluster outside Kubernetes by adding capacity to a storage pool, so that its logical volumes can grow beyond the current limit.
- [Operations / Scaling / Expanding a Storage Pool](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/scaling/expanding-storage-pool.md): Expanding a Storage Pool: Simplyblock is designed as on always-on a storage system.
- [Operations / Data Protection](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/data-protection/index.md): Protect the data of a simplyblock cluster outside Kubernetes with snapshot backups to S3-compatible object storage and asynchronous replication.
- [Operations / Data Protection / Backup and Recovery](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/data-protection/backup-recovery.md): Snapshot-based backup and recovery to Amazon S3 or S3-compatible object storage on plain Linux, managed through the Simplyblock CLI.
- [Operations / Data Protection / Asynchronous Replication](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/data-protection/asynchronous-replication.md): Asynchronous replication between simplyblock clusters: disaster recovery, cross-cluster volume migration, failover, and failback.
- [Operations / Monitoring](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/monitoring/index.md): Monitoring the health, performance, and resource utilization of a Simplyblock cluster is crucial for ensuring optimal operation, early issue detection, and.
- [Operations / Monitoring / Cluster Health](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/monitoring/cluster-health.md): Cluster Health: A simplyblock cluster consists of interconnected management nodes (control plane) and storage nodes (storage plane) working together to deliver.
- [Operations / Monitoring / Logical Volume Conditions](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/monitoring/lvol-conditions.md): Logical Volume Conditions: Logical volumes are the core storage abstraction in simplyblock, representing high-performance, distributed NVMe block devices backed.
- [Operations / Monitoring / Accessing I/O Stats (sbctl)](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/monitoring/io-stats.md): Accessing I/O Stats: Simplyblock's tool provides the option to retrieve some extensive I/O statistics.
- [Operations / Monitoring / Alerting](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/monitoring/alerts.md): Simplyblock uses Grafana to configure and manage alerting rules By default, Grafana is configured to send alerts to Slack channels.
- [Operations / Monitoring / Accessing Grafana](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/monitoring/accessing-grafana.md): Accessing Grafana: Simplyblock's control plane includes a Prometheus, Grafana, and Graylog installation Grafana retrieves metric data from Prometheus, including.
- [Operations / Monitoring / Accessing Graylog](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/monitoring/accessing-graylog.md): Accessing Graylog: Simplyblock's control plane includes a Prometheus, Grafana, and Graylog installation Graylog retrieves logs for all control plane and storage.
- [Operations / Security](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/security/index.md): Secure a simplyblock deployment outside Kubernetes: authenticate and encrypt the NVMe-oF transport, encrypt volumes, and isolate tenants from each other.
- [Operations / Security / Host Authentication and Encryption](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/security/authentication-encryption.md): Simplyblock provides host access control, DH-HMAC-CHAP authentication, and TLS/PSK encryption for NVMe-oF connections.
- [Operations / Security / Multi-Tenancy](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/non-kubernetes/operations/security/multi-tenancy.md): Multi-Tenancy: Simplyblock is designed to support secure and efficient multitenancy, enabling multiple independent tenants to share the same physical.

## Tutorials

- [Tutorials](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/tutorials/index.md): The tutorial section provides a collection of tutorials, introduction videos, and step-by-step guides to help users get started with simplyblock.
- [Introduction to Simplyblock](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/tutorials/simplyblock-intro.md): Video introduction to Simplyblock architecture, platform capabilities, and core concepts for building high-performance cloud-native storage.
- [Deploying OpenBao as a KMS](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/tutorials/openbao-kms.md): Step-by-step tutorial that deploys OpenBao on Kubernetes and wires it into a simplyblock cluster as the external key management system for volume encryption.

## Reference

- [Reference](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/index.md): Reference: Simplyblock provides multiple interfaces for managing and interacting with its distributed storage system, including the command-line interface (CLI).
- [API / Developer SDK](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/api/index.md): API / Developer SDK: Simplyblock offers a comprehensive API to manage and automate cluster operations.
- [API / Developer SDK / API Reference](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/api/reference.md): Interactive Simplyblock API reference generated from OpenAPI, with endpoint details, request/response schemas, and integration-oriented examples.
- [CLI / Command-line interface](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/index.md): CLI / Command-line interface: Simplyblock provides a feature-rich CLI (command line interface) client to manage all aspects of the storage cluster.
- [CLI / Command-line interface / Storage Node Commands](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/storage-node.md): Aliases: sn
- [CLI / Command-line interface / Cluster Commands](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/cluster.md): Cluster Commands
- [CLI / Command-line interface / Logical Volume Commands](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/volume.md): Aliases: lvol
- [CLI / Command-line interface / Control Plane Commands](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/control-plane.md): Aliases: cp mgmt
- [CLI / Command-line interface / Storage Pool Commands](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/storage-pool.md): Aliases: pool
- [CLI / Command-line interface / Snapshot Commands](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/snapshot.md): Snapshot Commands
- [CLI / Command-line interface / Backup Commands](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/backup.md): Backup Commands
- [CLI / Command-line interface / QoS Commands](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/qos.md): QoS Commands
- [CLI / Command-line interface / FDB Backup operations](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/cli/db-backup.md): FDB Backup operations
- [Simplyblock Operator](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/operator/index.md): The simplyblock Kubernetes operator manages simplyblock storage clusters, storage nodes, pools, logical volumes, and devices using Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs).
- [Simplyblock Operator / Simplyblock Operator Reference](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/operator/reference.md): Reference for Simplyblock Operator Custom Resource Definitions (CRDs).
- [Simplyblock Helm Chart Reference](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/kubernetes/index.md): Kubernetes Helm Chart Parameters: Simplyblock provides a Helm chart to install one or more components into Kubernetes.
- [Limits](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/limits.md): Hard object limits and vCPU-dependent resource limits of simplyblock storage nodes and clusters: subsystems, namespaces, objects per node, and sizing rules.
- [Upgrade Matrix](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/upgrade-matrix.md): Upgrade Matrix: Simplyblock supports in-place upgrades of existing clusters. However, not all versions can be upgraded straight to the latest versions.
- [Supported Linux Distributions](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/supported-linux-distributions.md): Supported Linux Distributions: Simplyblock requires a Linux Kernel 5.19 or later with NVMe over Fabrics and NVMe over TCP enabled.
- [Supported Linux Kernels](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/supported-linux-kernels.md): Supported Linux Kernels: Simplyblock is built upon NVMe over Fabrics. Hence, it requires a Linux kernel with NVMe and NVMe-oF support.
- [NVMe Low-Level Format](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/nvme-low-level-format.md): Guide to NVMe low-level formatting for Simplyblock environments, including when formatting is needed and how to prepare devices safely.
- [Troubleshooting](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/troubleshooting/index.md): Troubleshooting: Simplyblock is designed as a system for minimal manual intervention.
- [Troubleshooting / Control Plane](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/troubleshooting/control-plane.md): Control Plane: Symptom: FoundationDB error. All services that rely upon the FoundationDB key-value storage are offline or refuse to start.
- [Troubleshooting / Storage Plane](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/troubleshooting/storage-plane.md): Storage Plane: Symptom: After a fresh deployment, the cluster cannot be activated.
- [Troubleshooting / Kubernetes CSI](https://docs.simplyblock.io/latest/reference/troubleshooting/simplyblock-csi.md): Kubernetes CSI: Controller Plugin runs as a StatefulSet and manages volume provisioning and deletion. Node Plugin runs as a DaemonSet and handles volume attachment and mounts.
